intro: Mr Lee missed the meeting, Tom can't read the notice in your kos, and Emma wants to know what an arisan is. In this lesson you sum up texts and conversations for other people, explain Indonesian rules, menus and news in English, and explain Indonesian words like mudik that have no English word. Warm-up: how would you explain gotong royong to a foreign friend?
teachingNotes: Build on a2-mediation-messages (passing on a short message; the key facts of a notice: what, when, where, what to do; skipping Dengan hormat / Atas perhatiannya; air mati → There's no water) and on the chain: b1-reported-speech-intro (said / told + person, verb one step back: is → was, can → could, will → would, don't → didn't, past → had + past participle; today → that day) and b1-reading-articles (main idea vs details). Recap each in a line; the new skill is the summary. A summary for someone else = the main point FIRST, then the 2–3 key facts the listener needs (often what, when, where and what they have to do), in your own words, much shorter than the original, and accurate: no wrong facts, nothing new, not your opinion. Useful starters: Basically, … / In short, … / The main point is (that) … / The email says (that) …

Text vs conversation: a text that still exists (email, article, notice) → says + present (The email says the office is closed on Friday). A conversation that is over → said / told + backshift (Pak Hasan said the client was happy, but she wanted a lower price). A same-day report of something still true may stay in the present (Pak Hasan says the client wants a lower price): accept both in open answers; questions only test clear cases. Common errors: copying or translating sentence by sentence (as long as the original); starting with a detail or a reason instead of the main point; leaving out what the listener has to do, or the day / time; changing a fact (Tuesday ↔ Thursday); adding an opinion; 'He said me that…' (→ told me / said); 'Pak Hasan said I will send…' (→ he would send).

Explaining an Indonesian source (kos rules, office announcements, menus, short news) to Tom, Emma or Mr Lee: explain what it means for THEM (can / can't, have to, when, where, how much), not every word. Patterns: dilarang … → You can't … / No + -ing (No smoking); wajib / harus … → You have to …; mohon / harap … → Please …; paling lambat tanggal 5 → by the 5th; a di- verb → say who does it (Pagar dikunci pukul 22.00 → They lock the gate at 10 p.m.; Sampah dibuang hari Selasa → Put your rubbish out on Tuesdays) or use close/open (The gate closes at ten). The passive is NOT in this lesson's chain: don't teach it; accept it if the learner uses it correctly. News: main point first (The news says …), then the numbers. Prices: Rp25.000 → Rp25,000 (English writes thousands with a comma), twenty-five thousand rupiah. rubbish (British) = trash / garbage (American). Common errors: word for word ('Forbidden cooking in room', 'The garbage throws', 'Guest prohibited to sleep'), keeping every formal phrase, reading Rp25.000 as twenty-five.

Menus: dish names are names. Keep nasi goreng, gado-gado, rendang, soto, then explain (Nasi goreng is fried rice, usually with egg and chilli; Gado-gado is vegetables with egg and peanut sauce; Rendang is like a beef curry, but drier; Soto is a kind of soup). Without the name Emma can't order. Don't translate names literally: nasi kucing is not 'cat rice' (a very small portion of rice with sambal and a little fish); es teh tawar = iced tea with no sugar, not 'tasteless'. pedas = spicy (hot can also mean very warm, so spicy is clearer); manis = sweet.

Words with no English word: keep the Indonesian word, explain it with It's a kind of + noun / It's when + person + verb / It's like X, but … , then add 1–2 key facts. Facts to get right: mudik = travelling back to your hometown (kampung halaman) for Lebaran (Eid, the holiday at the end of Ramadan); arisan = a regular meeting of friends, neighbours or colleagues, everyone pays the same amount into a pot and each time one name is drawn and that person takes all the money, until everyone has had it once (no interest, it's also social); gotong royong = people working together for the community for free (kerja bakti = cleaning the street or drains together, often on a Sunday morning); kos = a room you rent by the month, often with a shared bathroom and kitchen, the owner (ibu kos / bapak kos) often lives there and makes the rules; ojek = a motorbike taxi, ojek online = booked on an app; angkringan = a street food cart from Central Java and Yogyakarta, cheap snacks, nasi kucing and hot drinks, open until late; THR = a holiday bonus, by law at least one month's salary for workers with 12+ months, paid at least a week before the religious holiday (for most people Lebaran). Common errors: 'It's kind of gathering' (missing a; kind of without a = agak), 'It's when people going' / 'It's when go back' (needs a person + verb), one vague word ('Arisan is a party'), literal names ('cat rice', 'village fried rice'), 'mudik = go home' (sounds like going home after work).

Limits: no relative clauses (a gathering where…, a cart that sells…): use two short sentences or with; no passive; no second conditional; reported questions and orders are not drilled. Grading: any short natural answer with the key facts is right; partial credit when one key fact is missing; a word-for-word translation that is unclear loses most of the credit; an answer in Indonesian shows understanding but asks for English.

keyPoints.title: A good summary: the main point + key facts
keyPoints.explanation: A summary gives someone the main point first, then the 2–3 key facts they need (often what, when, where and what to do), in your own words and much shorter than the original. Leave out greetings, examples and small details; never add facts or your opinion. For a text you can still read, use says + present (The email says…). For a conversation that's over, use said / told and move the verb one step back (Pak Hasan said he was busy).

examples.en: Basically, the email says the lift is broken until Friday.
examples.id: Intinya, email itu bilang liftnya rusak sampai Jumat.

examples.en: Sari told me she was sick, so she couldn't finish the report.
examples.id: Sari bilang ke aku dia sakit, jadi dia tidak bisa menyelesaikan laporannya.

examples.id: Singkatnya, Pak Hasan bilang desainnya bagus sekali, tapi terlalu mahal.

id.title: Ringkasan yang baik: inti + fakta penting
id.explanation: Ringkasan memberi orang lain intinya dulu, lalu 2–3 fakta penting yang mereka perlukan (sering: apa, kapan, di mana, dan apa yang harus dilakukan), dengan kata-katamu sendiri dan jauh lebih pendek dari aslinya. Lewati salam, contoh dan detail kecil; jangan menambah fakta atau pendapatmu. Untuk teks yang masih bisa dibaca, pakai says + bentuk sekarang (The email says…). Untuk percakapan yang sudah lewat, pakai said / told dan mundurkan kata kerjanya satu langkah (Pak Hasan said he was busy).

keyPoints.title: Explaining an Indonesian text in English
keyPoints.explanation: Explain what the text means for the listener (what they can or can't do, when, where, how much), not every word. dilarang → You can't… / No + -ing; wajib → You have to…; mohon / harap → Please…; a di- verb → say who does it (They lock the gate at 10 p.m.). On a menu, keep the dish name and explain it. Prices: Rp25.000 → Rp25,000.

examples.en: No smoking. / You can't smoke here.
You have to pay the rent by the 5th of every month.
examples.id: Pembayaran sewa paling lambat tanggal 5 setiap bulan.

examples.en: Nasi goreng is fried rice, usually with egg and chilli.
examples.id: Nasi goreng: nama tetap, lalu jelaskan isinya.

id.title: Menjelaskan teks berbahasa Indonesia dalam bahasa Inggris
id.explanation: Jelaskan apa arti teks itu bagi pendengarnya (apa yang boleh atau tidak boleh, kapan, di mana, berapa), bukan setiap kata. dilarang → You can't… / No + -ing; wajib → You have to…; mohon / harap → Please…; kata kerja di- → sebutkan siapa yang melakukannya (They lock the gate at 10 p.m.). Di menu, nama makanannya tetap, lalu jelaskan. Harga: Rp25.000 → Rp25,000.

keyPoints.title: Explaining a word with no English word
keyPoints.explanation: Keep the Indonesian word, then explain it with a pattern: It's a kind of + thing; It's when + person + verb; It's like … , but … . Add one or two key facts (when, who, why). Don't translate names word by word: nasi kucing isn't 'cat rice'.

examples.en: Angkringan is a kind of food cart. It sells cheap snacks and hot drinks until late at night.
examples.id: Angkringan: gerobak makanan murah yang buka sampai larut malam.

examples.en: Gotong royong is when neighbours work together for free.
examples.id: Gotong royong: tetangga bekerja bersama tanpa dibayar.

examples.en: A kos is like a shared house, but you rent only one room.
examples.id: Kos: mirip rumah bersama, tapi kamu hanya menyewa satu kamar.

id.title: Menjelaskan kata yang tidak ada padanannya dalam bahasa Inggris
id.explanation: Pertahankan kata Indonesianya, lalu jelaskan dengan pola: It's a kind of + benda; It's when + orang + kata kerja; It's like … , but … . Tambahkan satu atau dua fakta penting (kapan, siapa, kenapa). Jangan terjemahkan nama kata per kata: nasi kucing bukan 'cat rice'.

material.title: A good summary for someone else

blocks.text:
At A2 you passed on short messages and the key facts of a notice. Now the texts and conversations are longer: a long email from HR, an article, a 30-minute meeting. Your colleague doesn't want every word. They want a **summary** (*ringkasan*): the short version.

A good summary is:
- **Short**: much shorter than the original, often one to three sentences.
- **Complete**: the **main point** first, then the **2–3 key facts** the listener needs (often what, when, where, and what they have to do).
- **Accurate**: no wrong facts, nothing new, and not your own opinion.
- **In your own words**: don't copy sentence after sentence.

You know the main point from the reading lesson: it's the one big message of the text (like *kalimat utama*). Greetings, examples, reasons and small details can usually go.

Before you start, ask: **Who is it for, and what do they need to know or do?** Tom, back from leave, needs the new deadline. He doesn't need the story of the meeting.

id.text:
Di A2 kamu menyampaikan pesan pendek dan fakta penting dari sebuah pengumuman. Sekarang teks dan percakapannya lebih panjang: email panjang dari HR, sebuah artikel, rapat 30 menit. Rekan kerjamu tidak perlu setiap kata. Mereka perlu **ringkasan** (*summary*): versi pendeknya.

Ringkasan yang baik itu:
- **Pendek**: jauh lebih pendek dari aslinya, sering hanya satu sampai tiga kalimat.
- **Lengkap**: **inti** (*main point*) dulu, lalu **2–3 fakta penting** (*key facts*) yang dibutuhkan pendengarnya (sering: apa, kapan, di mana, dan apa yang harus dilakukan).
- **Akurat**: tidak ada fakta yang salah, tidak ada yang baru, dan bukan pendapatmu sendiri.
- **Dengan kata-katamu sendiri**: jangan menyalin kalimat demi kalimat.

Kamu sudah kenal *main point* dari pelajaran membaca: itu satu pesan besar dari teksnya (seperti *kalimat utama*). Salam, contoh, alasan dan detail kecil biasanya boleh dibuang.

Sebelum mulai, tanya dulu: **Untuk siapa, dan apa yang perlu dia tahu atau lakukan?** Tom, yang baru kembali dari cuti, perlu tahu tenggat barunya. Dia tidak perlu cerita lengkap rapatnya.

rows.en: Basically, the office is closed on Friday.
rows.id: Intinya, kantor tutup hari Jumat.
rows.note: Basically, … = here comes the main point

rows.en: In short, the new app is good, but it's slow.
rows.id: Singkatnya, aplikasi barunya bagus, tapi lambat.
rows.note: In short, … = to say it in a few words

id.note: In short, … = singkatnya, dalam beberapa kata

rows.en: The main point is that we need more staff.
rows.id: Intinya, kita butuh lebih banyak staf.

rows.en: The email says we have to finish the report by Monday.
rows.id: Di email itu tertulis kita harus menyelesaikan laporannya paling lambat hari Senin.
rows.note: a text you can still read: says + present

id.note: teks yang masih bisa dibaca: says + bentuk sekarang

blocks.text: **The copy trap.** Many learners copy or translate a text sentence by sentence. That isn't a summary: it's as long as the original. Try this: read the text, put it away, and say the main point in one sentence. Then look at the text again for the key facts (days, times, numbers, names): those you must get exactly right.

id.text: **Jebakan menyalin.** Banyak pelajar menyalin atau menerjemahkan teks kalimat demi kalimat. Itu bukan ringkasan: panjangnya sama dengan aslinya. Coba begini: baca teksnya, singkirkan, lalu ucapkan intinya dalam satu kalimat. Kemudian lihat lagi teksnya untuk fakta penting (hari, jam, angka, nama): bagian itu harus benar-benar tepat.

blocks.prompt: Which is the best summary of this email for Tom? 'Hi everyone! As you know, our team has grown a lot this year, and the 4th floor is now too small. Good news: from 1 March we move to the 7th floor. Please pack your desks by 27 February. Thanks!'
options: Our team has grown a lot this year, and the 4th floor is too small.
From 1 March we're on the 7th floor, so pack your desk by 27 February.
From 1 March we move to the 4th floor, and the new office is great.
blocks.explain: It has the main point (the move to the 7th floor from 1 March) and what Tom has to do (pack by 27 February). The first option is only the reason, a detail. The third gets the floor wrong and adds an opinion (great).

id.prompt: Mana ringkasan terbaik dari email ini untuk Tom? 'Hi everyone! As you know, our team has grown a lot this year, and the 4th floor is now too small. Good news: from 1 March we move to the 7th floor. Please pack your desks by 27 February. Thanks!'
id.explain: Ringkasan ini berisi intinya (pindah ke lantai 7 mulai 1 Maret) dan apa yang harus Tom lakukan (berkemas paling lambat 27 Februari). Pilihan pertama hanya alasannya, sebuah detail. Pilihan ketiga salah lantai dan menambahkan pendapat (great).

id.title: Ringkasan yang baik untuk orang lain

material.title: Summing up a conversation: said, told, one step back

blocks.text:
When the text is still there (an email, an article, a notice), use **says** and the present: *The email **says** the office **is** closed on Friday.* The text says it now, every time you read it.

When you sum up a **conversation that's over** (a call, a meeting, a chat in the pantry), use what you learnt in the reported speech lesson: **said** (no person after it) or **told** + a person, and move the verb **one step back**: *is → was*, *can → could*, *will → would*, *don't → didn't*.

Pak Hasan in Monday's meeting: *'The client is happy, but she wants a lower price. I'll send a new offer tomorrow.'*
Your summary for Emma on Friday: *Pak Hasan **said** the client **was** happy, but she **wanted** a lower price. He **would** send a new offer the next day.*

Notice: the summary keeps the main point and the key fact, and it leaves out nothing important. If you report it the **same day** and it's still true, the present is fine too: *Pak Hasan says the client wants a lower price.*

id.text:
Kalau teksnya masih ada (email, artikel, pengumuman), pakai **says** dan bentuk sekarang: *The email **says** the office **is** closed on Friday.* Teks itu "berkata" begitu sekarang, setiap kali kamu membacanya.

Kalau kamu meringkas **percakapan yang sudah lewat** (telepon, rapat, ngobrol di pantry), pakai yang kamu pelajari di pelajaran reported speech: **said** (tidak diikuti orang) atau **told** + orang, dan mundurkan kata kerjanya **satu langkah**: *is → was*, *can → could*, *will → would*, *don't → didn't*.

Pak Hasan di rapat hari Senin: *'The client is happy, but she wants a lower price. I'll send a new offer tomorrow.'*
Ringkasanmu untuk Emma hari Jumat: *Pak Hasan **said** the client **was** happy, but she **wanted** a lower price. He **would** send a new offer the next day.*

Perhatikan: ringkasan itu tetap memuat intinya dan fakta pentingnya, tanpa melewatkan hal penting. Kalau kamu melapor **di hari yang sama** dan isinya masih benar, bentuk sekarang juga boleh: *Pak Hasan says the client wants a lower price.*

rows.en: Sari told me she couldn't come because she was sick.
rows.id: Sari: 'Aku nggak bisa datang, aku sakit.'

rows.en: Budi said the meeting room was too small.
rows.id: Budi: 'Ruang rapatnya terlalu kecil.'

rows.en: Bu Ani told the team she would be back on Monday.
rows.id: Bu Ani: 'Saya kembali hari Senin.'
rows.note: English needs will here (I'll be back), so: will → would

id.note: Bahasa Inggris memakai will di sini (I'll be back), jadi: will → would

rows.en: The article says young people are choosing healthy food.
rows.id: Artikel itu bilang anak muda sekarang memilih makanan sehat.

blocks.text: **said me ✗ → told me.** Indonesian *bilang* covers both, so learners write *He said me that…* Use **told me** or **said (that)**. And change the words for people: *Pak Hasan said I will send a new offer* ✗ sounds like YOU will send it. Say **he would send**.

id.text: **said me ✗ → told me.** Kata *bilang* dalam bahasa Indonesia mencakup keduanya, jadi pelajar sering menulis *He said me that…* Pakai **told me** atau **said (that)**. Dan ubah kata untuk orangnya: *Pak Hasan said I will send a new offer* ✗ kedengarannya seperti KAMU yang akan mengirim. Katakan **he would send**.

blocks.prompt: Last week at lunch Dimas said: 'I can't join the futsal team. My knee hurts.' Today Tom asks why Dimas isn't playing. Which summary is right?
options: Dimas said me he can't join because my knee hurts.
Dimas said he couldn't join because his knee hurt.
Dimas told he couldn't join because his knee hurt.
blocks.explain: said + no person, can't → couldn't, my → his, and hurts → hurt (the past of hurt is also hurt). The first has said me and keeps my; the third has told with no person after it.

id.prompt: Minggu lalu waktu makan siang Dimas bilang: 'I can't join the futsal team. My knee hurts.' Hari ini Tom bertanya kenapa Dimas tidak main. Ringkasan mana yang benar?
id.explain: said + tanpa orang, can't → couldn't, my → his, dan hurts → hurt (bentuk lampau hurt juga hurt). Pilihan pertama memakai said me dan tetap my; pilihan ketiga memakai told tanpa orang setelahnya.

id.title: Meringkas percakapan: said, told, mundur satu langkah

material.title: Explaining an Indonesian text: rules, notices, news

blocks.text:
Tom lives in your kos, Emma eats with you at a warung, and Mr Lee reads the office group but not Indonesian. When they ask *What does it say?*, don't translate every word. Ask: **What does it mean for them?** What can or can't they do, when, where and how much? Then say it in short, natural English, and skip the formal openings and closings (*Dengan hormat*, *Atas perhatiannya*).

Indonesian rules and notices use formal words that sound strange in English word by word. Use these everyday patterns:
- **dilarang …** → **You can't …** or **No + -ing** (*No smoking*, *No parking*)
- **wajib / harus …** → **You have to …**
- **mohon / harap …** → **Please …**
- **paling lambat tanggal 5** → **by the 5th**
- A **di-** verb (*dikunci, dibuang, dibayar*) often sounds best with a person: *Pagar dikunci pukul 22.00* → ***They lock** the gate at 10 p.m.* Or use *close* or *open*: *The gate **closes** at 10 p.m.*

For **news**, start with the main point, like in the reading lesson, then add the numbers: *The news says the KRL fare goes up on 1 May. A trip of 25 km costs Rp5,000.*

id.text:
Tom tinggal di kosmu, Emma makan bersamamu di warung, dan Mr Lee membaca grup kantor tapi tidak bisa bahasa Indonesia. Saat mereka bertanya *What does it say?*, jangan terjemahkan setiap kata. Tanyakan: **Apa artinya bagi mereka?** Apa yang boleh atau tidak boleh mereka lakukan, kapan, di mana, dan berapa? Lalu katakan dalam bahasa Inggris yang pendek dan wajar, dan lewati pembuka dan penutup resminya (*Dengan hormat*, *Atas perhatiannya*).

Aturan dan pengumuman dalam bahasa Indonesia memakai kata-kata resmi yang terdengar aneh kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata. Pakai pola sehari-hari ini:
- **dilarang …** → **You can't …** atau **No + -ing** (*No smoking*, *No parking*)
- **wajib / harus …** → **You have to …**
- **mohon / harap …** → **Please …**
- **paling lambat tanggal 5** → **by the 5th**
- Kata kerja **di-** (*dikunci, dibuang, dibayar*) sering paling enak didengar kalau ada orangnya: *Pagar dikunci pukul 22.00* → ***They lock** the gate at 10 p.m.* Atau pakai *close* atau *open*: *The gate **closes** at 10 p.m.*

Untuk **berita**, mulai dengan intinya, seperti di pelajaran membaca, lalu tambahkan angkanya: *The news says the KRL fare goes up on 1 May. A trip of 25 km costs Rp5,000.*

rows.en: No smoking. / You can't smoke here.
rows.id: Dilarang merokok.

rows.en: You have to pay the rent by the 5th of every month.
rows.id: Pembayaran sewa paling lambat tanggal 5 setiap bulan.

rows.en: They lock the gate at 10 p.m.
rows.id: Pagar dikunci pukul 22.00.
rows.note: a di- verb: say who does it (they)

id.note: kata kerja di-: sebutkan siapa yang melakukannya (they)

rows.en: Please keep the kitchen clean.
rows.id: Mohon jaga kebersihan dapur.

rows.en: The office is closed on Friday. We're back on Monday.
rows.id: Diberitahukan bahwa kantor libur pada hari Jumat dan masuk kembali hari Senin. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.
rows.note: skip the formal opening and closing

blocks.text: **Word-for-word traps.** *Dilarang parkir di depan pagar* is not *Forbidden parking in front of fence*: say **You can't park in front of the gate** or **No parking in front of the gate**. *Harap tenang* is not *Hope calm*: say **Please be quiet**. And *sampah* is **rubbish** in British English, **trash** or **garbage** in American English.

id.text: **Jebakan kata per kata.** *Dilarang parkir di depan pagar* bukan *Forbidden parking in front of fence*: katakan **You can't park in front of the gate** atau **No parking in front of the gate**. *Harap tenang* bukan *Hope calm*: katakan **Please be quiet**. Dan *sampah* dalam bahasa Inggris British adalah **rubbish**, dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika **trash** atau **garbage**.

blocks.prompt: Your kos notice: 'Pembayaran listrik paling lambat tanggal 10 setiap bulan.' What do you tell Tom?
options: Payment of electricity is latest on the 10th.
You have to pay for electricity by the 10th of every month.
You can pay for electricity after the 10th of every month.
blocks.explain: It says who pays (you) and turns paling lambat into by the 10th. The first is word for word and unclear; the third changes the meaning (after instead of by).

id.prompt: Pengumuman di kosmu: 'Pembayaran listrik paling lambat tanggal 10 setiap bulan.' Apa yang kamu katakan ke Tom?
id.explain: Kalimat ini menyebut siapa yang membayar (you) dan mengubah paling lambat menjadi by the 10th. Pilihan pertama kata per kata dan tidak jelas; pilihan ketiga mengubah artinya (after, bukan by).

id.title: Menjelaskan teks berbahasa Indonesia: aturan, pengumuman, berita

material.title: Menus: keep the name, then explain

blocks.text:
Dish names are names: **nasi goreng** stays *nasi goreng*, just like *pizza* stays *pizza* in Indonesian. If you only say *fried rice*, Emma can't find it on the menu or order it. So say the name, then explain it: what's in it, and is it spicy or sweet?

Be careful with names that sound funny word by word: *nasi kucing* is not 'cat rice', and *es teh tawar* is not 'tasteless ice tea'.

Prices: Indonesian writes **Rp25.000**, but English uses a comma for thousands: **Rp25,000**, said *twenty-five thousand rupiah*. (In English a dot is for decimals: 2.5 = *two point five*.)

id.text:
Nama makanan adalah nama: **nasi goreng** tetap *nasi goreng*, sama seperti *pizza* tetap *pizza* dalam bahasa Indonesia. Kalau kamu hanya bilang *fried rice*, Emma tidak bisa menemukannya di menu atau memesannya. Jadi sebutkan namanya, lalu jelaskan: isinya apa, pedas atau manis?

Hati-hati dengan nama yang jadi lucu kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata: *nasi kucing* bukan 'cat rice', dan *es teh tawar* bukan 'tasteless ice tea'.

Harga: bahasa Indonesia menulis **Rp25.000**, tapi bahasa Inggris memakai koma untuk ribuan: **Rp25,000**, dibaca *twenty-five thousand rupiah*. (Dalam bahasa Inggris, titik dipakai untuk desimal: 2.5 = *two point five*.)

rows.en: Nasi goreng is fried rice, usually with egg and chilli.
rows.id: Nasi goreng biasanya pakai telur dan cabai.

rows.en: Gado-gado is vegetables with egg and peanut sauce.
rows.id: Gado-gado: sayuran dengan telur dan bumbu kacang.

rows.en: Rendang is like a beef curry, but drier.
rows.id: Rendang mirip kari sapi, tapi lebih kering.

rows.en: Nasi kucing is a very small portion of rice with sambal and a little fish.
rows.id: Nasi kucing: nasi porsi kecil dengan sambal dan sedikit ikan.

rows.en: Es teh tawar is iced tea with no sugar.
rows.id: Es teh tawar: es teh tanpa gula.

rows.en: It costs twenty-five thousand rupiah.
rows.id: Harganya Rp25.000.

blocks.text: **hot or spicy?** *Pedas* = **spicy**. *Hot* can mean spicy, but it can also mean very warm, so **spicy** is clearer: *The sambal is very spicy.* *Tidak pedas* = **not spicy**, and *pedas sedang* = **medium spicy**.

id.text: **hot atau spicy?** *Pedas* = **spicy**. *Hot* bisa berarti pedas, tapi bisa juga berarti panas, jadi **spicy** lebih jelas: *The sambal is very spicy.* *Tidak pedas* = **not spicy**, dan *pedas sedang* = **medium spicy**.

blocks.prompt: Emma points at 'Sayur asem' on the menu. Which explanation helps her most?
options: Sayur asem is a kind of vegetable soup with a sour taste, from tamarind.
Sayur asem is a kind of sweet cake.
blocks.explain: It keeps the name, says what kind of dish it is (a soup) and why it's sour. 'Sour vegetable' is word for word: Emma still doesn't know it's a soup. The third is simply wrong.

id.prompt: Emma menunjuk 'Sayur asem' di menu. Penjelasan mana yang paling membantunya?
id.explain: Penjelasan ini mempertahankan namanya, menyebut jenis makanannya (sup) dan kenapa rasanya asam. 'Sour vegetable' itu kata per kata: Emma tetap tidak tahu bahwa itu sup. Pilihan ketiga jelas salah.

blocks.text:
Some Indonesian words have no English word: *mudik*, *arisan*, *gotong royong*, *kos*, *angkringan*, *THR*. Don't look for one word. Keep the Indonesian word, and explain it with one of three patterns:
- **It's a kind of** + a thing: *Angkringan is **a kind of** food cart.*
- **It's when** + a person + a verb: *Gotong royong is **when** neighbours **work** together for free.*
- **It's like** + a thing from their country + **but** + the difference: *A kos is **like** a shared house, **but** you rent only one room.*

Then add one or two key facts: when, who, why. Two short sentences are clearer than one long one.

**Grammar traps:** *It's a kind of* needs **a** (*It's kind of sweet* means *agak manis*!). *It's when* needs a person and a verb: *It's when go back* ✗, *It's when people going* ✗ → *It's when people **go** back*. And one vague word isn't an explanation: *Arisan is a party* doesn't say anything about the money.

id.text:
Beberapa kata Indonesia tidak punya padanan dalam bahasa Inggris: *mudik*, *arisan*, *gotong royong*, *kos*, *angkringan*, *THR*. Jangan mencari satu kata. Pertahankan kata Indonesianya, lalu jelaskan dengan salah satu dari tiga pola:
- **It's a kind of** + benda (= semacam): *Angkringan is **a kind of** food cart.*
- **It's when** + orang + kata kerja (= saat/ketika): *Gotong royong is **when** neighbours **work** together for free.*
- **It's like** + sesuatu dari negara mereka + **but** + bedanya (= mirip …, tapi …): *A kos is **like** a shared house, **but** you rent only one room.*

Lalu tambahkan satu atau dua fakta penting: kapan, siapa, kenapa. Dua kalimat pendek lebih jelas daripada satu kalimat panjang.

**Jebakan tata bahasa:** *It's a kind of* butuh **a** (*It's kind of sweet* artinya *agak manis*!). *It's when* butuh orang dan kata kerja: *It's when go back* ✗, *It's when people going* ✗ → *It's when people **go** back*. Dan satu kata yang kabur bukan penjelasan: *Arisan is a party* tidak menjelaskan apa pun soal uangnya.

rows.en: Mudik is when people travel to their hometown for Lebaran.
rows.id: Mudik: pulang ke kampung halaman saat Lebaran.
rows.note: Lebaran = Eid, the holiday at the end of Ramadan

id.note: Lebaran = Eid (Idulfitri), hari raya di akhir Ramadan

rows.en: Arisan is a kind of regular social gathering. Everyone pays money into a pot, and each time one person wins it all.
rows.id: Arisan: pertemuan rutin; semua menyetor uang, dan setiap kali satu orang mendapat semuanya.
rows.note: a pot = the money of the group

rows.en: Gotong royong is when people in a neighbourhood work together for free.
rows.id: Gotong royong: warga satu lingkungan bekerja bersama tanpa dibayar.
rows.note: kerja bakti = one kind: cleaning the street together

id.note: kerja bakti = salah satu bentuknya: bersih-bersih jalan bersama

rows.en: A kos is like a shared house, but you rent only one room, and the owner often makes the rules.
rows.id: Kos: mirip rumah bersama, tapi kamu hanya menyewa satu kamar, dan pemiliknya sering membuat aturan.

rows.en: An ojek is a kind of motorbike taxi. You sit on the back.
rows.id: Ojek: semacam taksi motor. Kamu duduk di belakang.
rows.note: ojek online: you book it on an app

rows.en: Angkringan is a kind of food cart from Central Java and Yogyakarta. It sells cheap snacks and hot drinks until late at night.
rows.id: Angkringan: gerobak makanan dari Jawa Tengah dan Yogyakarta, menjual camilan murah dan minuman panas sampai larut malam.
rows.note: two short sentences: what it is + key facts

id.note: dua kalimat pendek: apa itu + fakta penting

rows.en: THR is a holiday bonus, usually one month's salary. Companies pay it before Lebaran.
rows.id: THR (Tunjangan Hari Raya): bonus hari raya, biasanya satu bulan gaji, dibayar sebelum Lebaran.
rows.note: a bonus = extra money from your company

id.note: a bonus = uang tambahan dari perusahaan

blocks.text: **Don't over-translate.** *Mudik* is not just *go home*: that sounds like going home after work. *Lebaran* can stay *Lebaran*; add *Eid* once so Tom knows the holiday. Names of places and dishes (*angkringan*, *nasi kucing*, *Malioboro*) stay as they are; you explain them, you don't translate them.

id.text: **Jangan terlalu menerjemahkan.** *Mudik* bukan sekadar *go home*: itu kedengarannya seperti pulang kerja. *Lebaran* boleh tetap *Lebaran*; tambahkan *Eid* sekali supaya Tom tahu hari rayanya. Nama tempat dan makanan (*angkringan*, *nasi kucing*, *Malioboro*) tetap seperti aslinya; kamu menjelaskannya, bukan menerjemahkannya.

blocks.prompt: Your RT group says there's kerja bakti on Sunday. Mr Lee asks: What's kerja bakti? Which answer explains it best?
options: It's when neighbours clean the street and the drains together on a weekend morning, for free.
It's like an office job, but at home.
blocks.explain: It uses It's when + person + verb and gives the key facts: who (neighbours), what (clean the street and drains), when (a weekend morning) and that nobody gets paid. 'A kind of work' is too vague, and the third is wrong.

id.prompt: Grup RT-mu bilang ada kerja bakti hari Minggu. Mr Lee bertanya: What's kerja bakti? Jawaban mana yang paling jelas?
id.explain: Jawaban ini memakai It's when + orang + kata kerja dan memberi fakta pentingnya: siapa (tetangga), apa (membersihkan jalan dan selokan), kapan (pagi di akhir pekan), dan tidak ada yang dibayar. 'A kind of work' terlalu kabur, dan pilihan ketiga salah.

id.title: Kata yang tidak ada padanannya dalam bahasa Inggris

resources.title: How to Summarize
resources.note: James shows a simple step-by-step way to summarise what you read. It's all in English, a little above this lesson's level, and it's about written summaries of texts, not explaining Indonesian words.

id.note: James menunjukkan cara sederhana langkah demi langkah untuk meringkas bacaan. Seluruhnya berbahasa Inggris, sedikit di atas level pelajaran ini, dan membahas ringkasan tertulis dari teks, bukan cara menjelaskan kata-kata Indonesia.

flashcards.back: Basically, … / In short, … / The main point is (that) …
said / told + verb one step back: Sari told me she was sick.
No smoking. / You can't smoke here.
They lock the gate at 10 p.m.
It's a kind of … / It's when … / It's like …, but …

id.intro: Mr Lee tidak ikut rapat, Tom tidak bisa membaca pengumuman di kosmu, dan Emma ingin tahu apa itu arisan. Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar meringkas teks dan percakapan untuk orang lain, menjelaskan aturan, menu dan berita berbahasa Indonesia dalam bahasa Inggris, dan menjelaskan kata-kata Indonesia seperti mudik yang tidak punya padanan dalam bahasa Inggris. Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu menjelaskan gotong royong ke teman dari luar negeri?
suggestedQuestions: Apakah aku selalu harus mengubah tense saat meringkas percakapan?
Bagaimana menjelaskan kata seperti gotong royong dalam bahasa Inggris?
Apakah nama makanan Indonesia perlu diterjemahkan?

assessment.msum-1: Tom baru kembali dari cuti. Dia bertanya apa isi email dari HR ini: 'Dear all, our car park needs some repairs. The work starts next Monday and takes about two weeks. Until then, please park in the car park at Plaza Mentari, across the road. The company pays for it: just keep your parking ticket and give it to Bu Ani at the end of the week. Thank you for your understanding. — HR' Lengkapi ringkasanmu dengan apa yang harus Tom lakukan, dalam bahasa Inggris: Our car park is closed for about two weeks from next Monday, so ___
assessment.msum-2: Selasa lalu Pak Hasan bilang kepadamu di telepon: 'The client from Surabaya can't come on Thursday. She can come on Monday at ten, and she wants to see the new office.' Ringkasanmu untuk Emma: 'Pak Hasan said the client couldn't come on Thursday. She wanted to see the new office.' Fakta penting apa yang terlewat? Tulis dalam beberapa kata bahasa Inggris.
assessment.msum-3: Pengumuman di dinding kosmu: 'PERATURAN KOS: 1. Tamu dilarang menginap. 2. Tamu wajib pulang sebelum pukul 22.00. — Ibu Kos' Tetangga barumu, Tom, bertanya apa aturan tentang tamu. Jelaskan dalam satu atau dua kalimat pendek bahasa Inggris.
assessment.msum-4: Mr Lee melihat berita ini di TV kantor: 'Mulai 1 Desember, penumpang MRT Jakarta bisa membayar tiket dengan QRIS di semua stasiun.' Dia bertanya: What's the news? Jelaskan dalam satu kalimat pendek bahasa Inggris.
assessment.msum-5: Dua minggu sebelum Lebaran, Tom bertanya kenapa semua orang di kantor membicarakan tiket mudik. Lengkapi penjelasannya dalam bahasa Inggris: Mudik is when people ___ for Lebaran.
assessment.msum-6: Mr Lee membaca di grup kantor: 'THR cair minggu depan!' dan semua orang senang. Dia bertanya: What's THR? Jelaskan dalam satu kalimat pendek bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan: It's a kind of
assessment.msum-7: Kamu sedang di warung bersama Emma. Menunya: 'Ayam geprek (pedas, level 1–5) … Rp22.000 · Ayam bakar madu (manis, tidak pedas) … Rp25.000 · Mie goreng jawa (pedas sedang) … Rp18.000'. Emma tidak bisa makan makanan pedas. Menu mana yang sebaiknya dia pesan? Tulis namanya persis seperti di menu.
